issues.t: Worn valve seats cause misfires and lost compression
issues.sym: Check engine light, a shaky idle, misfires (often codes P0300 or P0304), weaker power, harder starting and worse fuel economy. It often shows up past 100,000 miles.
issues.why: The intake valve seats in the early 2.8L and 3.5L engines wear out too soon, so the valves no longer seal and a cylinder loses compression. GM extended the warranty on these engines to 7 years or 100,000 miles, which has now run out on every truck.
issues.next: Have a compression or leak-down test done when the misfire starts. A repaired or updated cylinder head usually fixes it; if the engine is badly worn, a replacement engine may make more sense.

issues.t: 4-speed automatic slips or loses gears
issues.sym: The engine revs but the truck doesn't speed up, shifts come late or hard, or the truck gets stuck in a low gear and won't shift into 3rd or 4th.
issues.why: The 4L60-E automatic used in these trucks wears its internal clutches and parts, especially with towing, heat or old fluid. Loss of 3rd and 4th gear is a classic failure of this transmission.
issues.next: Check the fluid level and smell. If it slips or won't shift, have it diagnosed before driving much farther, because more damage raises the rebuild cost.

issues.t: Blower fan works only on some speeds or not at all
issues.sym: The heater and A/C fan stops blowing, or works only on certain speeds (often only high). You may smell hot plastic near the passenger footwell.
issues.why: The blower motor resistor fails, and the heat can melt its wiring connector. This is the most-reported problem on first-generation Canyons, usually around 90,000 miles.
issues.next: Replace the resistor and check its connector for melting. If the connector is burned, replace it too, or the new resistor can fail again.

issues.t: Passlock security light and engine won't crank
issues.sym: The engine won't turn over, or it cranks and won't start, and a security or Passlock light shows on the dash. It may happen now and then at first, then every day.
issues.why: The anti-theft system stops seeing the right signal from the ignition, usually because the ignition switch or the Passlock sensor in the steering column has failed or corroded.
issues.next: A shop can read the security codes to confirm it. Replacing the ignition switch or the Passlock sensor usually fixes it; the parts are not expensive.

issues.t: Timing chain rattle at startup
issues.sym: A rattle from the engine for a few seconds after a cold start. If the chain stretches further you may see a check engine light, a rough idle, misfires or less power.
issues.why: The timing chain stretches or its tensioner loses pressure over time, especially when oil changes are skipped or the oil is low.
issues.next: Do not ignore a rattle that gets longer or louder. Have the codes checked; replacing the chain, guides and tensioner early costs far less than repairing a jumped timing chain.

issues.t: Cam phaser (VVT actuator) rattle and rough running
issues.sym: A rattle on startup, a check engine light with cam timing codes such as P0017, a rough idle or misfires.
issues.why: The variable valve timing actuator on the camshaft, or the oil control solenoid that feeds it, wears or gets clogged with sludge, so cam timing goes out of range.
issues.next: Have the codes read. Sometimes only the inexpensive solenoid is needed; a worn actuator costs more. Fresh oil at the right level helps prevent it.

issues.t: EVAP leak or gas cap check engine light
issues.sym: Check engine light, sometimes with a 'Check fuel cap' message. Codes are often P0455 or P0449/P0450. The truck drives normally.
issues.why: A worn gas cap that no longer seals, or a sticking EVAP vent valve or canister, lets the fuel vapor system fail its self-test.
issues.next: Make sure the cap clicks tight first. If the light comes back, have the code read; a new cap or vent valve is a cheap fix.

issues.t: Random electrical problems from corroded grounds
issues.sym: Power windows or locks quit, lights act up, gauges flicker, or the truck sometimes won't start, with no clear pattern.
issues.why: Ground wire splice packs under the hood corrode, and a weak body control module ground can cause several systems to misbehave at once.
issues.next: Have a shop check the battery, then the ground splices and body control module ground before replacing expensive modules.

issues.t: Frame and body rust
issues.sym: Bubbling paint and rust on the cab corners, rocker panels and bed, and scaly rust on the frame rails that can turn into holes.
issues.why: Salted winter roads and years of outdoor parking let rust take hold, especially on trucks used for work.
issues.next: Have the frame inspected on a lift, especially before buying. Frame holes are a safety problem and can fail inspection.

issues.t: Brake lights may fail or stay on (recall)
issues.sym: Brake lights don't come on when you press the pedal, or stay lit. The third brake light or cruise control may also stop working.
issues.why: Contamination in the brake lamp switch causes it to stick or lose contact. GM recalled 2004-2006 trucks and later 2004-2009 trucks in certain states for this.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. A GMC dealer replaces the switch free under the recall.

issues.t: Hood may be missing its secondary latch (recall)
issues.sym: Usually nothing until the main latch lets go; then the hood can fly open while driving.
issues.why: Some trucks were built without the backup hood latch required by federal rules.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. The dealer fixes it free.

issues.t: Rear axle pin can break and lock the rear wheels (recall)
issues.sym: A clunk or grinding from the rear axle; in the worst case the rear wheels lock up while driving.
issues.why: The cross pin inside the rear differential was not heat-treated correctly and can fracture.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. The dealer installs a new pin free.

issues.t: Power steering assist cuts out suddenly (recall)
issues.sym: Steering suddenly turns heavy, mostly at low speed, and a power steering warning appears.
issues.why: A poor electrical connection at the electric steering gear can drop the assist. GM recalled 2015 trucks twice for this.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. The dealer replaces the torque sensor cover free.

issues.t: Driver front air bag may not inflate correctly (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no warning before a crash.
issues.why: Several recalls covered the driver air bag: wiring that could upset deployment timing, an inflator that could separate, and second-stage inflation that may not work right in a high-speed crash.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. The dealer inspects, reprograms or replaces the air bag free.

issues.t: 8-speed automatic shudders at light throttle
issues.sym: A shake like driving over rumble strips at light throttle between about 25 and 80 mph, plus hunting between gears or clunky low-speed shifts.
issues.why: The torque converter clutch slips and chatters as the original transmission fluid breaks down. GM bulletin 18-NA-355 calls for a full fluid exchange with an updated fluid.
issues.next: Ask a dealer for the fluid exchange from the bulletin. Topping off with other fluid or additives won't fix it. If the shudder returns, the torque converter may need to be replaced.

issues.t: Diesel particulate filter and DEF warnings
issues.sym: Check engine light, a DEF or exhaust filter message, reduced power, smoke during cleaning cycles, or a speed-limit countdown.
issues.why: Short trips don't let the exhaust filter burn itself clean, and DEF quality and exhaust sensors fail. A failed sensor can also stop the cleaning cycle from running.
issues.next: Take the truck on a steady highway drive of 20 minutes or more when you can. If the warning stays, have the codes read; a sensor is cheaper than a new filter.

issues.t: Diesel warning lights and no-start from rubbed-through wiring
issues.sym: Several warning lights at once, a DEF message, a jumping oil pressure gauge, rough running, misfires, or the engine cranks and won't start.
issues.why: The engine wiring harness on the diesel can chafe through against nearby parts. GM bulletin 22-NA-003 covers finding and repairing the damaged section.
issues.next: Have a shop inspect the harness before replacing sensors or modules.

issues.t: DEF warning on freezing cold starts (emissions recall)
issues.sym: A DEF warning and a speed-limit message soon after starting in freezing weather.
issues.why: The DEF pump can start before the frozen fluid has thawed, so the system stops dosing for that drive.
issues.next: Check your VIN. The dealer reprograms the engine computer free under the emissions recall.

issues.t: High-pressure fuel pump can come loose and leak (recall)
issues.sym: A raw fuel smell from under the hood, or a fuel leak.
issues.why: The high-pressure fuel pump can come loose from its mounting and damage the fuel line next to it, which can leak fuel onto a hot engine.
issues.next: If you smell fuel, stop driving and have it towed. Check your VIN; the dealer replaces the pump and line free.

issues.t: Water leaks stain the headliner or wet the floor
issues.sym: Water stains on the headliner, damp carpet, or puddles on the floor after rain or a car wash.
issues.why: Water can get in at the roof ditch, rear glass, third brake light, windshield, cowl seam or A/C drain. GM issued a bulletin guiding technicians through these spots.
issues.next: Find and fix the leak soon, before mold or electrical damage sets in. A water test at a shop can pinpoint the source.

issues.t: Front brake calipers may leak fluid (recall)
issues.sym: A soft or sinking brake pedal, a brake warning light, or wet fluid at a front wheel.
issues.why: Air pockets in the caliper castings can let brake fluid seep out.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. The dealer inspects and replaces the calipers free.

issues.t: Turbo engine wiring harness rubs through
issues.sym: Check engine light with misfire or injector codes, a Reduced Power message, warning lights that seem unrelated, or a no-start.
issues.why: The engine harness can rub against the turbo actuator, wastegate linkage or a heat shield until a wire is damaged. GM bulletins PIE0808 and PIP6062 address it.
issues.next: Ask the dealer to inspect the harness near the turbo before replacing other parts.

issues.t: Coolant leak at the radiator hose quick-connect
issues.sym: Coolant drips at the front of the engine, a dropping coolant level, a sweet smell, or a low coolant warning.
issues.why: The seal inside the quick-connect fitting where the upper hose meets the radiator can leak. GM extended coverage to 5 years or 60,000 miles (bulletin N262546590).
issues.next: Keep an eye on the coolant level and don't let the engine overheat. If you're within coverage, the dealer replaces the seal free.

issues.t: Automatic emergency braking slams on for no reason (recall)
issues.sym: The truck brakes hard on an empty road, sometimes with a forward collision alert.
issues.why: The front camera module can falsely see an obstacle and trigger automatic braking.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. The dealer updates the camera software free.

issues.t: Front wheel hub bolts may be damaged (recall)
issues.sym: A clunk or wobble from a front wheel, or steering vibration that gets worse with speed.
issues.why: The hub bolts were over-tightened at the factory and can loosen or break, which can affect control of the truck.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. The dealer replaces the bolts free.

issues.t: Front seat belt buckle bolt may be loose (recall)
issues.sym: Usually nothing you can see; the buckle may feel loose.
issues.why: The bolt holding the front seat belt buckle may not have been tightened properly, so the belt might not hold in a crash.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. The dealer tightens the bolt free.

issues.t: Fuel pump lock ring may not be locked (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no sign; in a crash fuel could leak.
issues.why: The ring that holds the fuel pump into the tank may not have been fully locked during assembly.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. The dealer inspects and locks the ring free.

issues.t: Headlights may flicker (recall)
issues.sym: Headlights flicker while driving or parked, making it harder to see at night.
issues.why: A software error in the headlight control module causes the flicker.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. The dealer replaces the headlight module free.

issues.t: AT4X AEV passenger air bag may fire too hard (recall)
issues.sym: No warning before a crash.
issues.why: On AT4X AEV Edition trucks, wrong air bag software may fire the passenger air bag's stronger second stage when only the first stage is needed.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. The dealer updates the software free.

issues.t: Rough or clunky shifts when cold
issues.sym: Hard, clunky shifts or slamming downshifts from the 8-speed automatic, mostly before the truck warms up.
issues.why: Owners and technicians report it on this generation; GM has not named one cause.
issues.next: Ask the dealer to check for software updates. If shifts get worse or a transmission warning appears, have it diagnosed under warranty.

issues.t: Loud ticking from the 2.7L turbo under load
issues.sym: A harsh ticking from the engine, most noticeable when towing or climbing in 4-low.
issues.why: Owners report the 2.7L can be loud under heavy load; ticking on this engine family can come from the valvetrain.
issues.next: If the ticking is new, getting louder, or comes with a check engine light, have the dealer listen to it while the truck is under warranty.

issues.t: Service 4WD message or transfer case noise
issues.sym: A 'Service 4WD' message, noises from the transfer case, or four-wheel drive that won't engage or disengage.
issues.why: GM has a service bulletin for transfer case problems on this generation.
issues.next: Avoid relying on 4WD until it's checked. Have the dealer read the codes and check for the bulletin.
